August [Date], 2026

Harvard Pilgrim Health Care  
Appeals and Grievances Department  
1600 Crown Colony Drive  
Quincy, MA 02169  

Re: Appeal of Medical Necessity Denial  
Member: Morgan Alvarez  
Member ID: W375849485  
Plan: Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Commercial/ACA — Maine  
Requested service: Lumbar decompression/discectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Reference number: POC-FB8E2AE06A-30252  
Denial notice date: August 1, 2026  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030. The denial states that the submitted records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records demonstrate that I completed substantially more than the six-week conservative-treatment period described in the applicable Evolent lumbar-spine guideline and that the other clinical requirements are also met.

The policy document publicly identified for lumbar spine surgery is Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery, policy number Evolent_CG_3041766. The policy states that lumbar discectomy/microdiscectomy requires all of the following:

“Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities”

“Failure of conservative treatment for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months”

“Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual’s symptoms/signs”

The submitted records satisfy these requirements:

1. Conservative treatment was completed. I participated in supervised physical therapy for eight weeks, from May 15, 2026, through July 10, 2026, completing 20 visits. Treatment included core stabilization and lumbar flexibility exercises. The physical therapy discharge note documents this course. This exceeds the policy’s six-week requirement and occurred within six months before the August 1, 2026 denial.

2. Additional conservative treatment was unsuccessful. I used NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief. I also received a corticosteroid injection on May 14, 2026, which provided only four weeks of partial relief. Despite these measures and the completed physical-therapy program, my symptoms persisted.

3. The symptoms significantly impair daily activities. I have had progressive lower-back pain for 24 months, unrelieved by rest. I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I continue to experience radicular pain extending into the right calf.

4. The clinical findings correlate with the imaging. Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The May 29, 2026 lumbar MRI showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. These findings correspond to the right-sided radicular symptoms and neurologic findings.

The policy also describes failure of conservative treatment as including lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment, progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment, or a documented medical reason preventing participation. My records show completion of the full physical-therapy course, inadequate relief from NSAIDs, only temporary partial relief from injection treatment, and continuing functional impairment. Therefore, the denial reason is not supported by the clinical record.

There are no apparent additional risk factors requiring delay of treatment. I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a nonsmoker. The requested procedure is being recommended by Okafor, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, based on the documented disc extrusion, nerve-root compression, corresponding neurologic findings, and persistent disabling radicular symptoms.

I respectfully request that Harvard Pilgrim overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 63030. Please review the physical-therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, MRI report, examination findings, and the surgeon’s clinical documentation as part of this appeal.

If Harvard Pilgrim relied on criteria different from Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery, please provide the exact criteria, policy version, and clinical-review rationale applied to this request.

Please send the appeal determination in writing. Thank you for your prompt review.

Sincerely,

Morgan Alvarez
